title: GPU-Z — What GPU-Z does
description: GPU-Z by TechPowerUp is the standard lightweight utility for reading everything about a graphics card: chip, memory, clocks, temperatures, and power. It installs in seconds, needs no account, and is the first tool reviewers open when a new card lands on the bench.

title: GPU-Z — Installing GPU-Z
description: GPU-Z ships as a single small executable with an optional installer, and a portable build that runs from a USB stick. Because it touches only read-only hardware registers, it is safe to run on any machine you are evaluating.

title: GPU-Z — The Graphics Card tab
description: The Graphics Card tab is the card's identity card: name, GPU codename, process size, die size, transistor count, release date, BIOS version, device ID, and subvendor. When a used card's story sounds suspicious, this tab is where the truth check starts.

title: GPU-Z — Shaders, TMUs, and ROPs
description: Three numbers define a GPU's muscle: shaders (CUDA cores) do the math, TMUs filter textures, and ROPs write finished pixels. GPU-Z lists all three, and comparing them against the official spec instantly exposes a rebadged or fake card.

title: GPU-Z — Pixel and texture fillrate
description: Fillrate turns the unit counts into speed: pixel fillrate is ROPs times clock, texture fillrate is TMUs times clock. GPU-Z shows both, and this demo recomputes them from the raw counts so you can verify any card by hand.

title: GPU-Z — Hot spot temperature
description: Hot spot is the hottest single point on the die, always higher than the average GPU temperature, and it is the number that triggers throttling. A 10 to 15 C gap between GPU temp and hot spot is normal; a 30 C gap means the cooler mount or paste needs attention.

title: GPU-Z — Clocks: base, boost, current
description: GPU-Z separates the three clocks that matter: the guaranteed base, the rated boost, and what the card is actually running this second. A current clock stuck far below boost under full load is the classic symptom of heat or power throttling.

title: GPU-Z — The ? render test
description: The little question mark next to the PCIe bus field starts a 3D render test that forces the card out of its idle power state. Idle GPUs drop to fewer PCIe lanes to save power, so the test reveals the true negotiated link — x16 4.0 on a healthy desktop install.
